name: jags
desc: Just Another Gibbs Sampler for Bayesian MCMC simulation
why: Gibbs sampling for Bayesian MCMC is real statistical simulation you can run at home, with a fascinating old-school model language.

brief.what_it_is: JAGS (Just Another Gibbs Sampler) is a program for analysing Bayesian hierarchical models using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation. The homepage describes it as 'not wholly unlike BUGS', so it accepts models written in the BUGS language and runs the sampling engine on them. The homepage does not spell out the inputs and outputs beyond that, so the output format is not confirmed here. It is a command-line engine, indicated by the 'jags' executable.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives three aims: to provide a cross-platform engine for the BUGS language, to be extensible so users can write their own functions, distributions and samplers, and to serve as a platform for experimenting with ideas in Bayesian modelling.
brief.install_notes: The homepage points to SourceForge for source and to binary packages for Mac OS X and Windows. Linux binaries are distributed separately, with Debian and Ubuntu packages (credited to Dirk Eddelbuettel). A MacPorts port is maintained by Daniel Meliza. The development source is in a Mercurial repository on SourceForge. No runtime, account or configuration requirements are mentioned on the homepage.
brief.standout: It is a long-running open-source descendant of the BUGS tradition with an explicit goal of being extensible with user-written samplers and distributions, not just a fixed engine. The homepage frames it as a platform for experimenting with Bayesian modelling ideas as well as a tool for running them.
brief.status: Maintained, though the evidence is modest. The latest release is JAGS 4.3.2, dated 4 March 2023. The homepage was last updated 23 November 2023. I did not check the SourceForge project page for later commits.
brief.caveats: Licensed under GNU GPL version 2, so redistribution and modification carry GPL terms. The homepage says the Mac and Windows binaries come from third parties (Matt Denwood, Bill Northcott) and Linux binaries are distributed separately, so the Homebrew build is a separate channel. The homepage itself contains no usage examples, and I did not fetch the docs to see model syntax or a tutorial.
quotes: JAGS is Just Another Gibbs Sampler.
It is a program for analysis of Bayesian hierarchical models using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation not wholly unlike BUGS.
To have a cross-platform engine for the BUGS language
